title: Counit identification of a scalar support-triangle comparison
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$ be a closed immersion with complementary open $j:U\hookrightarrow P$, and let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Use ordinary etale module derived categories, the support triangles $i_*Ri_R^!L\to L\to Rj_{*,R}j^*L$ for $R=A,B$, and their counit/unit maps [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]. Write $T_W=-\otimes_A^LB_W$ and $\operatorname{Res}$ for exact restriction of scalars [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Let $L$ and $TL$, their closed exceptional images and the open terms in these triangles all be bounded below. Suppose the canonical projection $q_{i,Ri_A^!L}:T_Pi_{*,A}Ri_A^!L\to i_{*,B}T_ZRi_A^!L$ is an isomorphism. Suppose a morphism from the restriction $\operatorname{Res}(T_P(-))$ of the $A$-support triangle to the restriction of the $B$-support triangle has middle map the identity of $\operatorname{Res}(TL)$ and right map the canonical open coefficient projection. Identify its first source term using $\operatorname{Res}(q_i)$ and the canonical restriction/direct-image isomorphisms [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]. Then its first map is $i_*\operatorname{Res}(b_i)$, where
$$b_i:T_ZRi_A^!L\to Ri_B^!T_PL$$
is the $i_{*,B}\dashv Ri_B^!$ transpose of $T_P\epsilon_{i,A}\circ q_i^{-1}$. If the open coefficient projection is an isomorphism, then $b_i$ is an isomorphism. No injectivity after restriction of scalars and no flatness of $B/A$ is assumed.

source.place: Locality: identify the closed-factor comparison by supported/open orthogonality and the counit; extraction of old item Step 11 for thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity finite comparisons

proof.text: Work in $D(P_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Put $M=Ri_A^!L$, $N=Ri_B^!T_PL$, $S=\operatorname{Res}_P(T_Pi_{*,A}M)$, $F=\operatorname{Res}_P(i_{*,B}N)$, $K=\operatorname{Res}_P(T_PL)$ and $O=\operatorname{Res}_P(Rj_{*,B}j^*T_PL)$. The target triangle is $F\xrightarrow{e}K\to O\to F[1]$, with $e=\operatorname{Res}_P(\epsilon_{i,B})$. Both rows of the assumed comparison are distinguished: scalar extension is exact by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], restriction is exact by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], and exact restriction preserves triangles by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Their underlying support triangles and the counit and open-adjunction normalizations are supplied by [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]. Write $a:S\to F$ for the given first component and $s=\operatorname{Res}_P(T_P\epsilon_{i,A}):S\to K$. The first square of the hypothesized triangle morphism is exactly $e a=s$.

source.place: Counit-defined transpose and locality; explicit scalar support-triangle argument, setup

proof.text:
By the defining transpose under $i_{*,B}\dashv Ri_B^!$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient], the map $b_i:T_ZM\to N$ satisfies
$$\epsilon_{i,B}\circ i_{*,B}(b_i)=T_P\epsilon_{i,A}\circ q_i^{-1}.$$
Define $h=\operatorname{Res}_P(i_{*,B}b_i)\circ\operatorname{Res}_P(q_i):S\to F$. Applying the functor $\operatorname{Res}_P$ to the preceding equality and composing on the right with $\operatorname{Res}_P(q_i)$ gives $e h=s$, since $q_i^{-1}q_i=1$. This only applies a functor to an equality; it requires no injectivity of its map on morphisms.

source.place: Existence and uniqueness: defining counit equation for the transpose

proof.text:
The isomorphism $q_i$ identifies $S$ with $i_{*,A}\operatorname{Res}_Z(T_ZM)$. Here the interchange of $i_*$ and restriction is the sectionwise identity on module sheaves, applied termwise: both functors are exact, restriction by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] and closed direct image by [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization]. [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] makes this identity valid on all derived objects, even if $T_ZM$ is not bounded below. Therefore $j^*S=0$ by [lem-exc-derived-open-closed-vanishing]. The target open term is canonically $O\cong Rj_{*,A}\operatorname{Res}_U(j^*T_PL)$ by [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]; this use of the bounded-below comparison is permitted by the hypotheses on the $B$-triangle. The open adjunction $j^*\dashv Rj_{*,A}$ in [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] now gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(S[1],O)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j^*(S[1]),\operatorname{Res}_U j^*T_PL)=0.$$
Indeed $j^*$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so its derived functor commutes with shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], and $j^*(S[1])=(j^*S)[1]=0$.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), with etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04CA and the bounded-below coefficient comparison

proof.text: Steps 1 and 2 give $e(a-h)=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] to the backwards rotation $O[-1]\to F\xrightarrow{e}K\to O$ of the target triangle. Exactness says that $a-h:S\to F$ factors through $O[-1]$. The shift equivalence identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(S,O[-1])$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(S[1],O)$, which is zero by Step 3. Thus $a=h$. After identifying the source using $\operatorname{Res}(q_i)$, this reads $\operatorname{Res}_P(i_{*,B}b_i)$; naturality of the canonical restriction/direct-image comparison identifies it with $i_{*,A}\operatorname{Res}_Z(b_i)$, exactly the asserted first map. The source-side interchange is the termwise identity already checked in Step 3; the target uses the bounded-below canonical comparison of [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons], since $N$ is bounded below.

source.place: Tag 0149 (lemma-representable-homological), applied to the backwards-rotated target triangle

proof.text: Assume now the open coefficient projection is invertible. In the given morphism of distinguished triangles, the middle component is $1_K$ and the right component is this invertible projection after restriction. [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] implies that $a$ is invertible. Step 4 and invertibility of $q_i$ therefore show that $i_{*,A}\operatorname{Res}_Z(b_i)$ is invertible.

For a constant coefficient ring, [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization] gives the sheaf counit isomorphism $i^*i_*\cong1$ and exactness of $i_*$. The functor $i^*$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Apply these functors termwise and descend using [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. The same natural counit isomorphism gives $i^*i_*\cong1$ on ordinary derived categories, since it is an isomorphism of complexes in every representative. Applying $i^*$ to the invertible morphism of Step 5 and using its naturality gives that $\operatorname{Res}_Z(b_i)$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 08M3 (lemma-i-star-equivalence), constant-ring closed subtopos; termwise counit descent

proof.text: Exactness of restriction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identify $H^r(\operatorname{Res}_Z b_i)$ with $\operatorname{Res}_Z H^r(b_i)$ for every integer $r$, by computing on representatives (and hence also on roofs). These are isomorphisms by Step 6. Restriction keeps the same underlying sheaves and module maps [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. It reflects isomorphisms of module sheaves: the inverse of a bijective $B$-linear map is $B$-linear, since $f(bf^{-1}y)=by=f(f^{-1}(by))$. Thus every $H^r(b_i)$ is invertible. [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] makes $b_i$ invertible. This argument uses conservativity on objects and cohomology, not faithfulness on derived Hom sets, and imposes no flatness on $B/A$.

The delivery restricts the source to Res(T_P(-)). This matches what the sibling lem-pur-etale-kflat-support-comparison produces and what the citer lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons uses. Nothing is weakened, and the report names the change. Step checks: (1) T is triangulated by derived-change-of-rings (2), Res is exact and termwise, and the unbounded support triangles over any finite ring give e∘a=s. (2) The closed-ambient transpose gives e∘h=s. (3) Res i_*=i_* Res termwise (exact i_* from the trf closed-subtopos node, plus the factorization lemma), so this holds even for unbounded T_Z M. That gives j^*S=0. The open term goes through the D+ sbc comparison, which is valid because j^*TL is bounded below. So Hom(S[1],O)=0 by j^*⊣Rj_*. (4) Hom-exactness on the rotated triangle gives a=h. The target identification is via sbc (N is bounded below by hypothesis). (5) Two-of-three on the full triangle morphism. (6) i^*i_*≅1 termwise, then descended. (7) Res commutes with H^r and reflects module isomorphisms, then the cohomological iso criterion applies. Tested i=id, Z empty, A=B, and non-flat Z/4→Z/2 (unbounded T_Z M is handled termwise).
